skill.name: github-release-management
skill.description: Guides GitHub release planning, changelog generation, validation, publishing, monitoring, and rollback workflows using GitHub CLI and claude-flow examples.
skill.summary: Coordinate GitHub releases from version planning through validation, publishing, and rollback.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are markdown fences or expected GitHub release examples, so they were adjudicated as false positives. The audit confirms high-risk credential handling for GitHub and npm tokens, and adds a high-risk semantic finding for mutable npx package execution in release workflows.

remediation.issue: Mutable release tooling is executed with npx claude-flow@alpha in CI.
remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow to a reviewed version, use a lockfile or checksum, and avoid mutable dist-tags in release workflows.

remediation.issue: The workflow writes NPM_TOKEN into .npmrc before publishing.
remediation.suggestion: Use scoped npm automation tokens, prefer NODE_AUTH_TOKEN where possible, and remove .npmrc immediately after publishing.

remediation.issue: The workflow authenticates GitHub CLI with a write-capable GitHub token in shell.
remediation.suggestion: Use least-privilege workflow permissions, scope GH_TOKEN to the needed step, and avoid printing or storing token material.

remediation.issue: Release examples include package publishing, Docker publishing, deployment, and rollback actions.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run modes, explicit human approvals, protected environments, and documented rollback criteria before production use.

content.value_statement: Release work often spans versioning, changelogs, tests, artifacts, and rollback planning. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured GitHub release workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides draft release creation with GitHub CLI and generated notes.
Shows version bump, changelog, and release branch workflows.
Provides AI swarm patterns for release planning, testing, and deployment coordination.
Includes GitHub Actions examples for release and hotfix automation.
Documents validation, rollback, monitoring, and troubleshooting steps.
Covers multi-package and multi-repository release coordination.
limitations: Provides markdown examples, not a verified executable release system.
Assumes GitHub CLI, npm, Docker, and claude-flow tooling are available.
Requires review before publishing packages, tags, releases, or deployments.
Uses example versions, repository names, and workflow snippets that need adaptation.

use_cases.title: Plan a Standard Release
use_cases.description: Create a release plan with version changes, notes, validation tasks, and publishing checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Build a Release Workflow
use_cases.description: Adapt the GitHub Actions examples for artifact builds, security checks, package publishing, and monitoring.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Hotfix
use_cases.description: Use the hotfix workflow guidance to branch, test, publish, notify users, and monitor recovery.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Draft Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to prepare a draft GitHub release for version v1.4.0. Include title, notes outline, validation steps, and manual approval points.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Release Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to turn merged pull requests and commit summaries into release notes. Group features, fixes, breaking changes, and migration tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a CI Release Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a GitHub Actions release workflow with tests, security scanning, artifact upload, package publishing, and rollback validation.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Multi-Repository Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a synchronized release across frontend, backend, and CLI repositories. Include compatibility checks, sequencing, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: Prepare a patch release for v1.4.3 after three bug fixes and one documentation update.
output: Suggested patch version with release title.
Grouped changelog sections for fixes and documentation.
Validation checklist covering tests, build, and release review.

output_examples.input: Design a release workflow for npm and GitHub artifacts.
output: Workflow stages for checkout, dependency install, validation, artifact build, and publishing.
Security notes for scoped tokens, pinned tooling, and manual approvals.

output_examples.input: Plan an emergency hotfix for a critical production bug.
output: Fast validation path with critical tests and build checks.

best_practices: Review generated release notes, changelogs, and version changes before publication.
Pin release tools and dependencies before running CI automation.
Use least-privilege tokens and clean temporary credential files after publishing.
anti_patterns: Running publish or deployment steps without a dry run or approval.
Copying example workflow permissions without reducing scope.
Using mutable tool versions like alpha tags in production CI.

faq.question: Does this skill create releases automatically?
faq.answer: It provides release workflow guidance and command examples. The user or agent still decides when to execute release actions.

faq.question: Which tools does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes GitHub CLI, npm, Docker for some examples, and claude-flow commands for swarm coordination examples.

faq.question: Can it support monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes multi-package release coordination and version alignment examples for monorepos.

faq.question: Does it store credentials?
faq.answer: The skill itself is documentation. Some workflow examples handle tokens, so teams should scope tokens and clean credential files.

faq.question: Can it generate changelogs?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes changelog workflows based on pull requests, commits, labels, and release ranges.

faq.question: How should teams use it safely?
faq.answer: Pin tooling, use least-privilege credentials, review generated notes, and require approvals before publish or deployment steps.
